full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 25-3-99 passed by the learned Second Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin/Commercial Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 104 of 1998 reversing the judgment and decree dated 16-2-98 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge, Second Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 96 of 1995. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit on the ground that since registered lease deed was executed in favour of Alimuddin he did not acquire any title over the suit property late Alimuddin had no right to transfer the Ka schedule property to anybody and accordingly, the plaintiff did not acquire any legal character in the suit property. The learned Subordinate Judge who heard the appeal however allowed the appeal and decreed the suit holding that the deed ochhiatnama is valid and the plaintiff acquired title in the suit property by the same though there may be some irregularities. 

 8. As it appears that the trial Court dismissed the suit on the ground that there being no registered lease deed in favour of late Alimuddin, the plaintiff acquired no legal right by the deed dated 25-8-77 whereas the learned Subordinate Judge, who heard the appeal and decreed the suit on the ground that late Alimuddin after allotment of Ka schedule made in the year 1960, took possession of the same, erected structure thereon and remained in possession till 1979 and thereafter the heirs of late Alimuddin remained in possession till filing of the suit and so Alimuddin acquired legal right therein and accordingly, late Alimuddin also had the right to transfer his right, titles and interest in the suit property in Ka schedule property in favour of the plaintiff. Unfortunately, both the courts below did not look into the contents of the deed dated 25-8-77 which is Ext 2 and decide whether the said deed dated 25-8-77 was a deed of gift as termed in the plaint or a Ochhiatnama i.e. will, the implications of a gift and Ochhiatnama are quite different inasmuch as Mr Alimuddin could transfer his entire land to anyone by a deed of gift but he was not entitled to make a will in respect of more than one-third of his surplus property. 

 12. Regarding the genuineness of the deed dated 25-8-77 it appears that though the. defendant No. 1 raised the question of genuineness but he during the trial did not pray for producing any admitted signature of Late Alimuddin to enable the Court to compare those by itself or by handwriting expert. Further, since the defendant took the ground that late Alimuddin did not sign the will, the onus was open to the defendant to prove that late Alimuddin did not sign the same. So, steps for producing document with admitted signature of Late Alimuddin and examination of these signatures by Handwriting Expert or by the Court, should have been taken by the defendant No. 1. Thus, in any view of the matter, the statement of the deposition of the plaintiff to the effect that "I cannot say in which SR Office the deed was registered. I had been living with my husband in Dhaka since before 25-8- 77 AD including 25-8-77 AD do not by itself prove that Late Alimuddin on 26-8-77 did not execute the will in question. In view of above I am of the view that the impugned judgment and decree is to be modified to the effect that the plaintiff will be entitled to get declaration only in respect of 1/3rd share in the Ka schedule property. 

 13. In. the result, the Rule is made absolute in part without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 25-3-99 passed by the learned Second Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin/Commercial Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 104 of 1998 is accordingly, modified and the plaintiff will get decree in respect of one-third portion of schedule "Ka" property.
